name: SyncWith Marketing Analytics
description: SyncWith connects your marketing and commerce sources — Google Analytics 4, Meta (Facebook) Ads, Google Ads, Shopify and more — to Claude. Connect a source over OAuth, then run live queries in plain language: pull spend by campaign, sessions by landing page, orders by product, and compare periods without leaving the chat. It also reads the reports you've built in the SyncWith Google Sheets add-on, so you can summarize them and check data freshness. Read tools run without confirmation; actions like connecting a source or running a live query ask first. Requires a SyncWith account.

_published_faq.name: How do I add SyncWith Marketing Analytics to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add SyncWith Marketing Analytics to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.syncwith.com/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the SyncWith Marketing Analytics MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: SyncWith Marketing Analytics provides these MCP tools: list_accounts, list_connectors, list_fields, list_reports, query, read_report, start_connect, and submit_feedback.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to SyncWith Marketing Analytics?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 18, 2026, alternatives to SyncWith Marketing Analytics in sales-and-marketing on the Manufact MCP catalog include Griddo AX Docs, Rocket Sloth, Affonso.io, Datacircle, and Tolt.

_published_faq.name: Does SyncWith Marketing Analytics MCP require authentication?

acceptedAnswer.text: SyncWith Marketing Analytics requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.
SyncWith Marketing Analytics is developed by SyncWith Inc.. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
